newsitem.title: USA: Natgas nearby futures end lower, AGAs seen neutral.
newsitem.headline: Natgas nearby futures end lower, AGAs seen neutral.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Wednesday in a moderately active session, with front months undermined most of the day by technical selling and profit taking despite a firmer cash, industry sources said.
November slid five cents to close at $2.575 per million British thermal units. December settled 5.7 cents lower at $2.676. Others ended mixed, with 1998 contracts gaining.

"The market is ready to pay up for gas if the weather warrants it, but there's no (cold) weather yet," said one Houston-based trader, adding Wednesday's AGA report was within expectations and viewed as neutral.

AGA said U.S. natural gas stocks rose last week by 57 bcf to 84 percent of capacity, in line with an earlier Reuters poll showing most expected a 50-55 bcf weekly build. Overall, stocks are 256 bcf or nine percent below year-ago levels, with the bulk of the deficit, or 150 bcf, in the producing region.
NYMEX ACCESS natgas prices showed little reaction to the storage data, with November still quoted about two cents below the day-session close at $2.55.

Technically, traders still pegged November support in the $2.51 area, with December support seen in the mid-$2.50s. While November did not settle below support, some chartists still viewed today's lower close after an early rally to a new high as a possible reversal.
And with little extreme weather on the horizon, some expected physical and paper prices to remain on the defensive until more winter-like temperatures arrive to tighten the balance.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices gained more than five cents Wednesday to the mid-to-high $2.50s. Midcon pipes were up about a nickel to the mid-$2.40s. New York city gate gas gained several cents to the mid-$2.90s or better.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip slipped 2.5 cents to $2.285. NYMEX said 51,792 Hub contracts traded, down from Tuesday's revised tally of 62,683. NYMEX November Hub natgas expires Friday, October 25.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled one cent higher at $1.105, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX November Alberta natgas expires Tuesday, October 29.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded but November finished unchanged at $2.38. NYMEX November Permian natgas expires Tuesday, October 29.

On the KCBT, November closed three cents lower at $2.40, while deferreds ended steady to down one-half cent. The East/West spread narrowed by two cents to 17.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT November natgas expires Monday, October 28.
